drug_class: Antiviral medication (nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor)
purpose: Entecavir is used to treat chronic hepatitis B, a viral infection that affects the liver. It helps reduce the amount of hepatitis B virus in your body and lowers the risk of serious liver damage over time. It does not cure hepatitis B, but it helps keep the virus under control.
how_it_works: The hepatitis B virus needs to make copies of itself to keep infecting your liver cells. Entecavir works by blocking a key tool the virus uses to copy its genetic material. Think of it like jamming the virus's copy machine so it cannot reproduce as easily, giving your immune system and liver a chance to recover.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well. Some common side effects include headache, tiredness, dizziness, nausea, and diarrhea. These are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, because stopping it can cause a serious flare-up of hepatitis B that could harm your liver. If you also have HIV and it is not being treated, tell your doctor before starting entecavir. Rarely, it can cause a serious condition called lactic acidosis (a buildup of acid in the blood), so contact your doctor right away if you feel very weak, have unusual muscle pain, trouble breathing, or stomach discomfort. Also, use caution if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 0.5 mg taken by mouth once a day on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours before or after a meal). If you have had prior treatment with certain other hepatitis B medicines or have HIV, the dose may be higher (1 mg once daily). Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try to take it at the same time each day.
